findings.text: follow-on: _placed_worker_can_hold_memory asks the liveness reader with the pointer's pid only, while the pointer also records pid_start_time and the recovery path elsewhere compares the live process's start time against it to rule out pid reuse (reckon/crew/recovery.py:4958). A pid the kernel has since recycled by an unrelated process therefore reads alive and holds a seat. The direction is fail-safe and matches the classifier's own reader, so it is a follow-on rather than a defect, but a long-lived fleet on a shared workstation can accumulate a seat held by a stranger's pid.

follow-on: the node's cases are homogeneous — every pointer in each case is either placed or unplaced. The plan section's done-when also asks for the roster refusal asserted over a single population holding both placed and unplaced runs on one backend, which the node's own FENCE-EVIDENCE narrows away; that assertion is the section's and belongs to the merged-head or integration node the node's fence names as a separate dispatch.
